Checked the closing formula against R533: wi6xi2i4 = Felséged, with the same substitution recurring across the three Hentér letters.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): the interlinear decipherment copied verbatim from NOTES into texts/mnl-g15-d80-f38_decryption.md; no cipher transcription exists (project work).

Re-read brief b28, step 1: DECODE R496, R533, R534 re-fetched with the cookie (b28_fetch.py): no DOC_ attachment or comment; the text of paragraphs 3-4 is the contemporary interlinear on the leaf, legible at 2-3x on IMG_R496_I3689_P1.

Figures correct the interlinear: 'Magyar' -> jancsarsag, 'twrbabo' -> turbatio, 'naltatnak' -> componalodnak, 'zenenkedem' -> remenkedem; 'Felsegednek' -> Felsegedet.

Reading of paragraphs 3-4 aligned word by word with the decode (every word carried; 4 [?]; 6 look-alike letters); score 0.000 on the modern Hungarian list (unaccented 1700s spelling), 0.833 explicit holes; sentences hold. Entry set read, grade A.

outcome.method_basis: A contemporary interlinear Hungarian decipherment covers the cipher on the target folio itself (MNL OL G 15, fol. 38), unflagged by DECODE R496; it was read and checked against the sibling R533 closing formula.
outcome.fraction_read_source: Reading audit 22 Oct 2026: share of the interlinear that reads as sentences, paragraphs 1-2, about 9 of 17 lines of the normalized text (no cipher transcription, so no token count; estimated). texts.label: R496, Hentér to Rákóczi, Constantinople 8 July 1707: paragraphs 1-2
texts.summary: Mihály Hentér, Rákóczi's envoy at Constantinople, to Ferenc Rákóczi II, 8 July 1707: the pasha of Belgrade received Rákóczi's gift favourably and offered troops, gunpowder and grain if Rákóczi sent six or seven thousand men against the Serbs; Hentér pressed for the deputation to be heard by the grand vizier, whose audience was delayed amid confusion in the capital; he closes with a request about the liberation of a captive.
texts.note: Decryption = the interlinear Hungarian, normalized, copied from NOTES.md; some middle clauses are uncertain or unread (need a Hungarian palaeographer). No transcription of the cipher signs (project work); the archive does not allow the scans to be republished. This entry: paragraphs 1-2 (the Belgrade pasha's offer, the audience sought for the deputation), which read.

reading_review.note: Paragraphs 1-2 of the normalized interlinear read as Hungarian sentences (the pasha received the gift and offers help with troops, powder and grain; Hentér sought an audience for the deputation before the grand vizier) with two bracketed uncertain phrases. Paragraphs 3-4 are mostly [...] and are split off as decoded, not read.

texts.label: R496, paragraphs 3-4 (the delayed audience, the captive, the closing)
texts.summary: The audience would have been granted, but a disturbance (turbatio) broke out among the Janissaries; as the chief officials are being changed, Hentér must wait until matters settle; the audience was solicited twice more and the answer was 'habeant patientiam, vocabuntur ad praesentandas literas'; he is hopeful about the liberation of Rákóczi's captive and closes as his humble servant.

reading_review.note: Contemporary interlinear decipherment read on the DECODE image at 2-3x and checked word by word against the cipher decoded with the alphabet fixed by paragraphs 1-2 (cipher tsv); the figures correct the interlinear at four places (jancsarsag, turbatio, componalodnak, remenkedem). 6 letters on look-alike signs, 4 words [?]. Clean share 0.000 on the modern Hungarian list, 0.833 explicit holes (b17_score.py HOLES=1); the sentences hold.
